Folks — pulled together responses to the most sensitive sections and attached a PDF of the proposed final answers. Summary below (pulled into the spreadsheet placeholders):

1) Misuse monitoring and detection:
- Multi-layered detection: (a) model-level safety classifiers for toxic/illicit content; (b) behavioral heuristics for anomalous request patterns; (c) rate and pattern-based throttles per API key.
- Scoring & triage: requests receive a safety score; thresholds trigger automated mitigation (content filtering, request blocking) and flagging for human review for borderline/high-risk cases.
- Human review: triage team receives a queue with context (prompt, model output, metadata). Default SLA for initial human review: 8 business hours for high-priority flags; 48 hours for medium.

2) Policy controls / configuration:
- Customer-configurable guardrails: allowlist/blocklist tokens, regex filters, and response-sanitization hooks.
- Per-customer policy profiles: enforced at routing layer; can pin to private model variants when required.

3) Data & telemetry / retention:
- Request/response logs retained by default 90 days for hosted customers; Dedicated and Private customers can configure retention up to 24 months under contract.
- Sensitive PII redaction: automatic PII scrubbers applied at ingestion; customers can opt-in to raw logging for troubleshooting under strict access controls and contractual terms.

4) Incident & reporting workflow:
- Automated alerts to on-call and customer security contacts when aggregated risk exceeds thresholds.
- We provide machine-readable incident exports and incident timeline summaries.
- SOC2 and audit evidence: we can supply SOC2 Type II summary and control mappings; see attached audit summary.

5) Abuse mitigation playbook (attached):
- Stages: detect -> contain (rate-limit / block) -> investigate (human review) -> remediate (model routing / policy updates) -> notify (customer + regulators as required).

I've attached: Redwood_Content_Safety_Response_FINAL.pdf and abuse_mitigation_playbook.docx and SOC2_Type2_Audit_Summary_2024.pdf.

If this looks good I recommend sending the FINAL PDF and a 1-page executive summary to Rachel and proposing a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through our controls.

- Aditya

Hi Rachel / FinTechX security team —

Thanks for the questionnaire and timeline. Attached is our completed questionnaire (PDF) plus the executive summary and supporting evidence you requested. High level points:

- Detection & response: multi-layered automated scoring feeds an internal triage queue with human review for high-risk cases. Default review SLA is 8 business hours for critical flags; we can offer tighter SLAs on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Policy controls: per-customer policy profiles, token allow/block lists, and response sanitization hooks.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary, audit control mappings, and our abuse mitigation playbook are attached.
- Retention: hosted defaults = 90 days; Dedicated/Private configurable up to 24 months.

Attachments: Redwood_Content_Safety_Response_FINAL.pdf (completed questionnaire + answers), Redwood_Executive_Summary_Content_Safety.pdf (1 page), SOC2_Type2_Audit_Summary_2024.pdf (audit), abuse_mitigation_playbook.docx (playbook)

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute sync next week for a short walkthrough? I'm available Wed/Thu 9–12 PT. Also happy to provide a scoped Proof-of-Concept for the misuse detection pipeline if you'd like a short technical deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
